steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Put sweet potatoes in a medium saucepan; cover with water. Cook over medium-high heat until tender and easily pierced with a fork, 10 to 15 minutes. Drain and transfer to a large bowl.
Mash sweet potatoes with a fork. Add eggs; mix until well combined. Add sugar, milk, butter, vanilla extract, and salt; mix until smooth. Transfer to a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Mix brown sugar and flour together in a medium bowl. Cut in butter with a pastry cutter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs; don’t overmix. Stir in pecans. Sprinkle topping over sweet potato mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until topping is lightly browned, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Yummy Sweet Potato Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This creamy sweet potato casserole recipe has a smooth, buttery filling and crisp brown sugar-pecan topping for a crowd-pleasing holiday side you can prep ahead for Thanksgiving or Christmas.

video.description: No holiday dinner is complete without the addition of this classic casserole. In this video, the Allrecipes team shows you how to make a yummy sweet potato casserole with a chopped pecan topping. The buttery-sweet flavor and the crisp and crunchy texture make this cozy side dish a must-have for both Thanksgiving and Christmas!

review.reviewBody: Superb!! OK..I changed some things...added some things..made it MUCH BETTER!!! I am from Louisiana...so I grew up eating sweet potatoes year round. But holiday time always mean Sweet potato Casserole..this one is the closest to how my granny and mom made it. I used 3 BAKED sweet potatoes (I often double the recipe). For a single recipe I cut the sugar down to 1/4 cup and I double the vanilla up to 1 tsp. I use evaporated milk instead of regular milk. I add 1 tsp of cinnmon, 1/4 tsp of both ground clove and ground nutmeg. For the topping..I double the recipe even on the single recipe. Does that make sense?? LOL ENJOY!!!!

Delicious! For those watching sugar, I left the sugar out of the sweet potato portion (leaving it only in the topping) and it still tasted great. Aside from trying to cut down on sugar, I was looking forward to a less "sweet" side, letting the sweet potatoes speak for themselves (and not trying to compete w/the pumpkin pie!). The game-changer was that I also used an immersion blender. This made the casserole so light and fluffy, it was like eating air!
This is by far the best recipe for sweet potato casserole. It is absolutely delicious

I make this every year. My ingredients are the same, but for ease I cook my sweet potatoes in the Instant Pot 15 - 19 minutes depending on the size, natural release. No peeling, just slip the skins off, then mash, they are creamier to me. I take this to a potluck in a crockpot, I make the topping without the pecans, then toast them and sprinkle on just before serving, otherwise the pecans get gummy in the crockpot.

After reading reviews, I used this recipe, but used a 40 oz can of yams, drained well, and then mashed with a fork. I substituted Swerve brown sugar for the real thing. It made me nervous, but both the potato and the crumbly layer tasted normal. No bitter taste. I would not add or change a thing, it was tasty!

Super easy! I did add spices as Melissa’s review from 2007 suggested. I added 1tsp vanilla extract, used 1/4c sugar, 1tsp cinnamon roll, 1/4tsp clove & nutmeg plus more sprinkled. I didn’t have evaporated milk to use but will try that next batch. I thought the topping would be crispier than it was, going to double it next time. Added marshmallows at the end of baking for my kids. They loved them and husband approved of the tweaks with spices but agreed about the topping.

This is the sweet potato casserole I make that everyone says is my specialty. I do two things differently. I bake my potatoes in the oven and remove jackets when cool. Then proceed as the recipe does, whipping the potatoes in a mixer until fluffy. I also use pecan halves and toast them, then chop. People have been raving about this casserole since 2005 when I got the recipe from a coworker.

The All Recipe Team did not change the recipe & I only read their added comment after I had it in the oven. . There is not enough sweet potatoes for this size pan. They suggested you tripled the sweet potatoes & keep topping the same.
the recipe sounds good/average, but does anyone know how hard it is to cut raw sweet potatoes? I bake or boil mine with skin on, let them cool and then peel and mash.

I used 8 large sweet potatoes. Boiled them with skins on until they were soft to pierce with a fork. Drained and cooled. Skins came right off. Easy to mash. Did not double anything else. Followed recipe. Will definitely make again!

This was absolutely delicious! Made it for the first time for Thanksgiving dinner this year and everyone loved it. I added a little extra sweet potatoes, split into two 8 x 8, kept topping the same-added it to top of one. Added a few marshmallows mixed into the other. Added marshmallows to the op with a very small amount of brown sugar butter crumbled mixed with some caramel baking bits. But the crumble topping was sooooo good!
My family loves this recipe, it’s a must for all family gatherings
Family favourite!!
If you don't like sweet potatoes, you will after tasting these!!

Fabulous! Just made this for the third time. For my topping: oats, unsweetened shredded coconut, chopped pumpkin seeds, brown sugar, flour, cinnamon (and sometimes nutmeg), butter. Soooo yummy. Thanks to all for suggestions!

This recipe is amazing. I have to thank Tina for submitting it. This is the recipe I use all the time now. My family and friends ask for it constantly. . Thanks again Tina, and allrecipes for posting it. 😎
I added real maple syrup - about 2 tablespoons.
Made this many times except I used cashews vs pecans

I am 83, have cooked since I was three, southern style. but mostly for huge amounts, 50 to 150, and more. I now can't walk and have a wonderful caregiver to help with my crippled hands. I wish someone would make a whole session of tiny recipes for one or two people. It's much too expensive and way too difficult, and has too many leftovers that don't get eaten to cook like this anymore. My caregiver does not know how to cook and doesn't like to cook anything, so I thought we would work together. All recipe team, sure hope you read this. We need your help. I love the sound of this recipe because there are soo many ways to change it. I choose spam for my meat and left out sugar and added a little maple syrup. haven't eaten it yet, but sure it will be great, thank you.

Even my kids loved this recipe! I used 4 large sweet potatoes, reduced sugar to 1/4 cup, and doubled the vanilla up to 1 tsp. As another reviewer suggested, I added 1 tsp of cinnmon and 1/4 tsp of ground nutmeg. It turned out great and my kids gobbled it up!
